title: Humanitarianism as the canon's property doctrine
statement: The canon proposes humanitarianism — the abolition of outright ownership in favour of forty-nine-year leases, with inheritance ended and holdings returning to the collective — delivered as the second of the New Commandments in the 1973 contact; this record carries the proposal as canon-explicit normative content under the same is/ought policing as the government and economy records, with the biblical jubilee resonance registered as the canon's own frame.

includes: The proposal as stated: lease tenure in place of ownership, the forty-nine-year term, inheritance abolition, and its second rank among the New Commandments
The jubilee resonance: the term's biblical echo (the Levitical cycle) as the canon's own frame, registered without arguing the economics from the scripture
The normative-family position: fourth of the family (government 0032; economy 0033; ethics 0041), completing the New Commandments' institutional core
excludes: Endorsement or operationalization by the corpus
Transitional or legal design; no implementation is specified or defended
Identification with terrestrial land-reform programs; family resemblance is context
The movement's advocacy history, which is organizational

source_references.locator: The New Commandments: the humanitarianism commandment, its lease term and inheritance provision
Leviticus 25 (the jubilee cycle the term echoes) — the canon's frame, not the argument
The academic treatment of the doctrine

alternatives.statement: Lease-only tenure with abolished inheritance faces the standard incentive and capital-formation objections; the proposal names an allocation without an economics.
The jubilee frame romanticizes a Levitical institution whose own historicity and scope are debated; the echo lends antiquity, not feasibility.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0020 is revised in a way that affects provenance.
The canon's fuller context changes the proposal's terms.
Public prose begins endorsing, operationalizing, or arguing the economics from scripture, all of which this record excludes.
